title: State Assignment
toolchain: no code on screen. Check every state transition table, K-map grouping, Boolean simplification, self-start check (feed each unused state into the next-state logic until it reaches a used state or loops) and gate count by exhaustive enumeration in Python 3.11.9, standard library only (itertools.product over states and inputs): `python3 -I check.py`. The planner's results are in PLAN.md (Decisions, 'Checked'). No HDL or circuit simulator is installed (iverilog, yosys, ghdl, verilator, ngspice: none).

sources.note: Slides for the whole course (190 pp., two slides per page). This lecture is the whole 'Synchronous State Machines 2' section, pp. 132-143: state assignment, the divide-by-5 counter (sequential, sliding and shift-register assignments), one-hot encoding (traffic light), and the Tripos synchroniser (sequential and one-hot). pp. 120-131 ('Synchronous State Machines 1') are Lecture 9, which has no recording here: refresher only, from pp. 121-128 (FSM definitions, Moore schematic p. 122, the Moore example p. 123 that is the synchroniser with states A/B/C, the traffic light pp. 124-127, power-up and self-starting pp. 127-128). Already known from our L6: D = Q', synchronous counter design with K-maps, unused counts as don't cares, asynchronous preset/clear. pdftotext drops overbars and primes: read every formula from the rendered page (pdftoppm). p. 133 writes 'log2 m' without ceiling brackets

the recording (59:57). Frames show the four simulator demos (74HC74 D flip-flops with active-low S and R pins, 1 Hz clock, LEDs, a plot with the clock red and the output blue): seq_state_ass (D_a from a 74HC08 AND fed by the Q-bar outputs, 74HC86 XOR into b, 74HC08 AND into c, output from b), slide_state_ass (one 74HC08 AND into a, then wires a to b to c), shift_reg_state_ass (stuck at 00000; the lecturer stops the clock and presets d and e, giving 11000), one_hot (stuck at 0000; he presets a, the amber flip-flop, and two 74HC32 ORs light the lamps). p. 143's closing slide is on screen at ~00:59:48.
